blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Looped Transformers increase computation per token by repeatedly applying a shared backbone, offering a way to improve language modeling and downstream task performance at a fixed backbone parameter count. However, each loop depends on the preceding loop, so increasing recurrent depth also increases decoding latency. Existing approaches include Parallel Loop Transformers, which reduce latency by overlapping loop computation across token positions, but yield rapidly diminishing marginal accuracy gains at larger depths. To address this challenge, we introduce LoopFold, which folds computation at multiple recurrent depths into parallel batches for the same token prefix. A lightweight predictor estimates inputs to later loops so they can start before earlier loops finish. A corrector then refines the outputs of these later loops using newly available results from earlier loops. All components are trained jointly using only the final next-token prediction loss. In experiments with 1.4B models, deeper LoopFold configurations achieve progressively higher average zero-shot accuracy across eight tasks, rising from 53.41% to 56.38%. Vanilla looped models and PLT show limited gains over the same depth range. Compared with a nine-loop vanilla model, LoopFold uses five sequential stages and additional parallel computation to reduce decoding latency by 46%.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Looped Transformers increase computation per token by repeatedly applying a
shared backbone ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Geiping et al., 2025a ) . This
recurrent depth can improve language modeling and downstream task performance
at a fixed backbone parameter count ( Saunshi et al., 2025 ) . However, each loop depends on the preceding loop’s
output, so greater depth requires more sequential backbone stages and
increases the wall-clock time needed to generate each token.

blocks.en:
Existing approaches reduce decoding latency by overlapping recurrent
computation across token positions. Parallel Loop Transformers (PLT) shift
hidden states by one token between loops, allowing different loop depths to
run concurrently using states from neighboring tokens ( Wu et al., 2025 ) .
Adding loops initially improves accuracy, but the positional mismatch
persists at every loop and the marginal gains quickly diminish at larger
depths ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . Recurrent-depth parallel samplers refine
several token drafts in parallel, but reducing the number of recurrent refinement steps
between draft updates trades accuracy for faster decoding ( Geiping et al., 2025b ) . The challenge is to start later loops before
their inputs are available while still incorporating the results of
earlier loops.

blocks.en:
We introduce LoopFold to fold recurrent depth into parallel computation
by batching hidden states from different depths of the same token prefix.
Specifically, a lightweight predictor estimates the inputs to later loops, allowing them to
start before the preceding loops finish. After each batched evaluation, a corrector
uses the newly available earlier-loop results to refine outputs computed from
the estimated inputs. These corrected states feed the next stage, and
the deepest corrected state predicts the next token.

blocks.en:
With 1.4B models, LoopFold achieves lower PPL and higher mean zero-shot
accuracy as the target depth index increases
(Figures 3 and 4 ). At target depth index D = 9 D=9 , LoopFold requires only five sequential stages rather than nine, reducing latency by 46%. It improves accuracy on all eight evaluated tasks, with Avg-8 increasing by 2.20 percentage points relative to the vanilla looped model, at the cost of additional parallel computation.
At matched training backbone-compute budgets of 1.68 and 2.16 ZFLOPs, and
separately at comparable decoding latency, LoopFold achieves lower PPL and
higher mean zero-shot accuracy than vanilla looped models. LoopFold thus improves the use of recurrent computation in two complementary ways: it can yield better quality at a fixed total backbone budget, and it can exploit available parallelism to perform additional recurrent computation without proportionally increasing decoding latency.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Recurrent-depth language models increase computation by repeatedly applying
a shared transition, as in Universal Transformers ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ) .
Such looping can approach the accuracy of deeper models with untied layers
on arithmetic and question-answering tasks ( Saunshi et al., 2025 ) .
PonderLM changes the input passed between loops, feeding a probability-weighted
average of token embeddings into the next loop ( Zeng et al., 2026 ) . Geiping et al. (2025a) sample recurrent depths during training to support variable test-time computation. Ouro instead learns an input-dependent exit gate for adaptive recurrent depth ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) . Hidden Decoding takes a different route,
expanding each token into multiple embedding streams that the backbone
processes together, while retaining their intermediate KV states as context ( Liu et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
To shorten the sequential path between loops, PLT and recurrent-depth parallel
samplers overlap computation across token positions. PLT pipelines loop depths
using states shifted across token positions ( Wu et al., 2025 ) . Recurrent-depth parallel samplers accelerate decoding from pretrained
checkpoints by refining several token drafts concurrently, relying on
per-loop input injection and decodable intermediate states ( Geiping et al., 2025b ) .
LoopFold uses predicted inputs and output correction to run several
backbone loops in parallel for the same token prefix.

blocks.en:
Classical Parareal uses a fine propagator for accurate parallel local solves
and a cheaper coarse propagator for sequential correction, iterating toward
the fine propagator’s sequential solution ( Lions et al., 2001 ) . Neural variants replace or parameterize the coarse component with learned networks ( Lee et al., 2021 ) . Related methods parallelize network evaluation
through fixed-point or Newton iterations ( Song et al., 2021 ; Lim et al., 2024 ) ,
with SNLP using structured Jacobian approximations for Transformer layers ( Han et al., 2026 ) . LoopFold adapts parallel evaluation and correction to a
shared recurrent backbone. Its predictor initializes later-loop inputs once,
allowing several loops to run together, while its corrector incorporates
newly available earlier-loop states into the parallel outputs. Unlike
classical Parareal, which iteratively seeks to recover the sequential fine
solution, LoopFold learns a fixed-stage parallel computation optimized
directly for next-token prediction. Its objective is therefore not to match
the sequential recurrent trajectory, but to produce predictive states under
a constrained number of sequential stages.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: We evaluate LoopFold under three complementary comparison regimes. Matched-training-compute comparisons test whether LoopFold can improve model quality at the same total backbone budget. Comparable-latency comparisons test whether additional backbone evaluations can be shifted onto the parallel dimension to improve quality without increasing the number of sequential stages. Finally, matched-target-depth comparisons characterize quality when LoopFold reaches the same target depth index with fewer sequential stages. Because these regimes hold different quantities fixed, we report them separately rather than interpreting them interchangeably.
blocks.zh: 我们在三个互补的比较制度下评价环球银行。 匹配-训练-计算比较测试LoopFold能否在同一总骨干预算上提高模型质量. 可比性比较测试能否将更多的主干评价转向平行层面,以提高质量,同时又不增加相继阶段的数量。 最后,匹配目标深度比较在LoopFold达到相同目标深度指数,相继阶段较少时,定性. 由于这些制度有不同数量固定,我们分别报告,而不是相互解释。

Each schedule is trained separately with the same tokenizer, data order,
and training recipe. The learning rate warms up to 2 × 10 − 4 2\times 10^{-4} over the first 1% of steps, then follows cosine decay to 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} .
The ablations use 410M models trained on 25B tokens.

blocks.en: 4.6 KV Sharing Across Recurrent Stages
blocks.zh: 4.6 经常阶段的KV共享

blocks.en:
Although LoopFold decodes at latency close to a shallower vanilla looped
model, storing an independent KV cache for every recurrent evaluation adds
memory cost. We address this cost in the 1.4B 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 1+2+2+2 model at target
depth index D = 5 D=5 , comparing the default No KV sharing policy with
two reuse policies. First-KV reuse retains the KV tensors from the
first evaluation at each loop depth and reuses them in later stages,
reducing the seven independent caches to five. To incorporate later-stage
updates for recent tokens, Hard overwrite-64 additionally
refreshes the most recent 64 cached positions using newly computed
sequential states. Each variant uses the same cache policy in training
and inference.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced LoopFold to fold recurrent computation into parallel stages
using a jointly trained backbone, predictor, and corrector. Experiments show that
this design can improve language modeling and zero-shot downstream performance
with fewer sequential backbone stages, while the component analyses highlight
the importance of correction. These results suggest that recurrent depth
and sequential decoding depth need not coincide: additional recurrent
computation can be shifted onto the parallel dimension when provisional
states are subsequently corrected.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了LoopFold,将经常计算折叠成平行阶段
使用联合训练的骨干、预测器和校正器。 实验表明
这种设计可以改善语言模型和零镜头下游性能
减少连续主干阶段,而组成部分分析则突出
纠正的重要性。 这些结果表明,经常发生的深度
和顺序解码深度不需要重合:
计算可移到并行维度中
各州随后将予以纠正。

blocks.en: LoopFold reduces sequential depth at the cost of additional backbone computation and thus higher FLOPs. It also increases KV-cache requirements; although KV sharing mitigates this overhead, our experiments show a modest trade-off in quality and/or latency. Reducing these computational and memory costs while preserving the benefits of parallel recurrent evaluation remains an important direction for future work.
blocks.zh: LoopFold以额外的骨干计算成本降低顺序深度,从而降低FLOP. 它还增加了对KV-cache的要求;虽然KV共享可以减轻这种间接费用,但我们的实验显示在质量和/或耐用性方面略有权衡。 减少这些计算和内存费用,同时保留并行经常性评价的好处,仍然是今后工作的一个重要方向。
